newsitem.title: USA: Clinton stresses commitment to N.Ireland peace.
newsitem.headline: Clinton stresses commitment to N.Ireland peace.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he would continue to work to help bring peace to Northern Ireland, but stressed that "a genuine cessation of violence" was needed for the peace process to work.

"I will continue to do whatever I can to be of assistance to the Irish and the British governments as long as they work for peace in Northern Ireland and to the other parties who are committed to peace," Clinton said at a White House news conference.

"I think that we should continue to try, but it's obvious that there has to be a genuine cessation of violence and that all the parties have to be able to rely on one another not to start killing again, either in Northern Ireland or Great Britain, in order for this peace process to go forward," he said.
In the first news conference since his re-election on Tuesday, Clinton said he hoped the United States could contribute to the lasting resolution of the confliclt "in the next four years."
